pr_title: Consider error_trace supported by all endpoints
pr_body:
Closes #109612

I had a go at fixing this, I can see why `error_trace` wasn't included in the first place, the other `ALWAYS_SUPPORTED` parameters are all consumed by `AbstractRestChannel`. `error_trace` isn't consumed until we create the `RestResponse`, so it won't be listed as consumed when we check for unconsumed parameters.

There is API for specifying response parameters (which we exclude from the unconsumed check) but it's overridable, so I don't know the ideal place to put the parameter(s) that `RestResponse` consumes.

This is one approach, feel free to suggest a better one.
pr_comments: Hi @nicktindall, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: The `error_trace` parameter should be considered supported on all REST endpoints
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.14

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

N/A

### Problem Description

When a `RestHandler` specifies its set of `supportedQueryParameters`, incoming requests will be validated to ensure they contain only the supported set of parameters. 

There are some query parameters that are interpreted by the REST infrastructure and available on every endpoint. They are considered "supported" by every endpoint without every endpoint having to list them in their `supportedQueryParameters`. `error_trace` is missing from that set, [despite being available on every endpoint](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/common-options.html#common-options-error-options).

### Steps to Reproduce

Specify `supportedQueryParameters` for an endpoint. Send a request to that endpoint including `error_trace=true`.

The request will be rejected due to an unsupported parameter.

It should not be rejected.

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

review_comments: It felt right for `RestResponse` to specify which parameter(s) it consumed? not sure if this is the best way to go about it.
I think so - this is kinda short-term anyway whilst we look at consolidating the validation steps
